title: Jim Cramer Says “Buy Reddit” (RDDT)
detail:
Jim Cramer Says “Buy Reddit” (RDDT)
Syeda Seirut Javed
Sat, September 19, 2026 at 2:33 PM CDT 3 min read
RDDT
Trade Reddit on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

During the September 17 episode of Mad Money, a caller asked why Reddit, Inc. (NYSE:RDDT) has remained range-bound and gradually drifted downward despite a long-term bullish outlook. Jim Cramer replied:

Alright, my take is that this is a $29 billion company. I think that there are companies that would pay $40 billion for just the book of business they have and be able to train all their different viewers and readers. Buy Reddit, period, end of story. Buy Reddit.

Jim Cramer on Seanergy Maritime (SHIP): “I'd Be a Buyer”
Reddit Posts Strong Second-Quarter Growth

Reddit, Inc.'s (NYSE:RDDT) second-quarter results provide strong financial support for the growth argument. Revenue rose 61% year over year to $805 million, advertising revenue increased 64% to $762 million, and adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $343 million. Daily active uniques increased 18% to 130.3 million, while weekly active uniques rose 24% to 514.6 million. The company also forecast third-quarter revenue of $860 million to $870 million and adjusted EBITDA of $385 million to $395 million.

At the September 8 Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference, CEO Steve Huffman said, "What is most valuable to Reddit is bringing users into the Reddit ecosystem. We want to grow our direct user base. That is where our business lives." He also discussed the company's efforts to grow its direct user base and convert mobile-web users into app users.

Bear Case: Traffic and Valuation

A risk worth mentioning is the composition of Reddit, Inc.'s (NYSE:RDDT) user growth. U.S. daily active uniques increased 6% year over year to 53.2 million in the second quarter, while logged-in U.S. daily active uniques rose only 1% to 23.1 million. International daily active uniques increased 28% to 77.1 million. Reddit reported second-quarter average revenue per unique of $11.85 in the U.S., compared with $2.26 internationally. Huffman said on September 8 that "traffic that is logged out or transient is just less meaningful to us," while Reddit is focused on growing its direct user base. He also said the company was continuing to work on converting mobile-web users into app users.

Valuation seems to leave less room for a slowdown. The company closed at $152.83 on September 17, giving it a market capitalization of approximately $29.4 billion. It also has a forward P/E of 23.31 as of September 17. The company is also investing heavily in its product. Huffman said the company considers its feed technology roughly 12 to 18 months behind the state of the art and that improving the feed is among its most important priorities over the next 12 to 18 months.

title: What Happens To Reddit Stock If Search Keeps Sending Fewer People?
detail:
What Happens To Reddit Stock If Search Keeps Sending Fewer People?
Trefis Team
Fri, September 18, 2026 at 4:36 PM CDT 3 min read
RDDT
^GSPC
PINS
SNAP
GOOG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Reddit (RDDT) stock trades near $153, down about 43% over the past year while the S&P 500 returned 17%. The market has already decided something here is wrong. The advertising business is not the problem; it is still growing fast. The risk sits one step upstream, in where the next visitor comes from.

Reddit Is Earning More From The Users It Already Has

Revenue grew 61% in Q2 2026, to $805 million, its eighth straight quarter of growth above 60%. The profit behind it is new: an operating margin of 28.2% over the past twelve months, at the high end of its multi-year range, against a three-year average of -15.0%.

Management puts the growth down to both pricing and impressions, and average revenue per unique user rose 36% year over year. Reddit is charging more for the audience it already has, helped by ad tools like Reddit Max and by the Dynamic Product Ads catalog. Daily users barely moved: product work added them in Q2 2026, and a decline in search referrals took them back, even as weekly reach grew past half a billion.

But Reddit Is Getting Less Help From Search

Search referrals were volatile through Q2 2026, and more so late in it. Management says its visibility there is low and expects the volatility to continue. By the CEO's account, the older search links delivered far more value to Reddit and to publishers than AI Overviews has so far. Reddit's data licensing relationships cover training, grounding and use as a search index, and the CEO says whether Reddit keeps licensing at all has a wide range of outcomes.

Growth has already stepped down. Management guided Q3 2026 revenue to 47% to 49% growth, against 61% in Q2 2026 and close to 70% in each of the three quarters before that.

And Reddit Has To Build Its Own Front Door

Reddit's answer is to become a destination rather than a stop after a search result, and that work runs through the home feed. By the CEO's own account the feed is well behind: the models are much smaller than the state of the art, and they take in about 10% of the user activity available. Management frames it as a year of work.

There is early evidence it can work. New app user retention rose 50% year over year on a relative basis in Q2 2026, though management calls that a small base. Retention is the number to watch. The user picture is about to get harder to see too: Q2 2026 is the final quarter in which Reddit splits logged-in from logged-out daily users.

So how much should this worry you? The fall is already in the price, so slower growth in Q3 2026 is not the surprise. The open question is whether direct users grow fast enough to replace what search used to send. That question gets answered one quarter at a time. title: Reddit (RDDT) Could Be 51% Undervalued Following Its Recent Share Price Slide
detail:
Reddit (RDDT) Could Be 51% Undervalued Following Its Recent Share Price Slide
Simply Wall St
Fri, September 18, 2026 at 1:11 PM CDT 4 min read
RDDT
Trade Reddit on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Reddit (RDDT) is drawing attention after recent trading left the stock down 3% on the day and lower over the past month and past 3 months, prompting renewed questions about current investor sentiment.

At a share price of $152.83, Reddit has seen its short term share price return weaken, with the 90 day share price return down 12.65% and the 1 year total shareholder return down 43.54%. This suggests that momentum has been fading as investors reassess growth potential and risk.

Scan beyond Reddit and size up other beaten down opportunities using our hand picked list of 29 high quality undervalued stocks, which combine resilient cash flows with balance sheets many investors overlook.

For Reddit, a 43.54% slide in 1 year total shareholder return and a 12.65% drop over 90 days can signal either a business reality check or a sharp swing in mood. What picture do the current valuation markers present?

Most Popular Narrative: 51% Undervalued

At $152.83, the most widely followed narrative around Reddit points to a fair value of about $309.77 per share, framing recent weakness as a potential disconnect between price and the long term story.

Successful ad networks are driven fundamentally by usage. The best type of usage is on returning daily users usually measured by Daily Active Users. The higher the number of unique daily active users the higher the ad revenue generated on a per day basis.

See why 32 investors see Reddit as 51% undervalued.

According to kinnth, the narrative hinges on Reddit's reach and monetisation engine. The platform reported 126.8 million Daily Active Uniques in Q1 2026 with a 17% year over year increase, and revenue of $663 million in that quarter, which the narrative frames as evidence that engagement is increasingly being converted into advertising and data related income.

That story sits alongside Reddit's reported annual revenue of $2.78b and net income of $871.10m, which translate into a net margin of about 31.3%. For many investors, a business that is already profitable, operating at this level of scale, and still associated with high usage metrics, can justify a valuation view that looks past recent share price pressure.

The same narrative uses a discount rate of 8.68% and arrives at a fair value estimate of $309.77 per share, implying Reddit trades at roughly a 50.7% discount to that figure. That is a wide gap for a company where earnings are forecast, according to the provided statements, to grow 24.21% per year and revenue is projected to expand 21.6% annually, especially when the stock is already down 43.54% on a 1 year basis.

Making more money sounds like the obvious way to get ahead in your 20s. But earning it and actually building wealth with it can be two very different things.

A user asked wealthy people what they wished they had started earlier and what advice they would give someone in their 20s in a post on Reddit's r/wealth community.

"The problem wasn't earning it, it was keeping it," a commenter wrote.

Don't Miss:

Warren Buffett once said, "If you don't find a way to make money while you sleep, you will work until you die." Here's how you can earn passive income with just $100.

AI Needs More Power Than The Grid Can Easily Provide. This Startup Is Taking A Different Approach To Energy Storage.

A Higher Income Could Disappear Into A Better Lifestyle

That commenter said they spent their 20s trying to make as much money as possible, but some of it went toward bigger houses, nicer cars, private jets and other upgrades. Real estate and businesses eventually made them wealthy, yet they still wished they had put more into the stock market along the way.

"Whether that's real estate, individual stocks, or ETFs doesn't matter nearly as much as consistently adding to them," they wrote.

Another commenter had come to a similar conclusion after landing a well-paying job.

"Upgrading my lifestyle didn't make me happier, it just raised my standards," the person wrote. Instead, they said they now keep things that still work and put most of their excess income into investments, hoping to eventually cut back to part-time work and retire early.

Starting Earlier Left More Room For Time To Work

A commenter in their 30s said they bought their first stock and cryptocurrency at 21, and some of those investments later rose more than 50 times in value.

"People that started even a few years later, now have to do a lot of catch up to get there," they wrote.

Trending: There's More Than One Way To Put Cash To Work. Some Accredited Investors Are Looking Beyond Savings Accounts.

But another commenter didn't think those early years should be spent only saving and investing.

"Save money… the compounding effects (aka rule of 72) are amazing!" the person wrote. But they didn't suggest spending an entire 20s preparing for some distant future. The same commenter urged younger people to travel, go on adventures and try new things, adding that "those experiences in your 20s are compounders too!"
